name: Distributed Nervous System Redundancy
description: Introduces a distributed network of neural ganglia throughout the body — concentrated clusters of nerve tissue in the torso, pelvis, and upper limbs that can take over basic autonomic function if the brain or spinal cord is damaged. The modification does not create consciousness outside the brain; it creates a biological backup system that maintains heartbeat, breathing, and basic motor function during neurological emergencies. If the primary spinal cord is severed, the distributed ganglia can maintain organ function and crude limb movement for 2–4 hours — enough time for emergency medical intervention. The modification is inspired by octopus distributed neural architecture, where two-thirds of neurons are in the arms rather than the central brain. Helix Biosystems positions it as the ultimate insurance against the most feared injuries in a violent city.
source_organism: Octopus vulgaris (common octopus, distributed nervous system), Asterias rubens (common starfish, neural regeneration)
procedure: Systemic neural retroviral treatment with ganglion seeding, 12 sessions over 8 months
expression_time: 8–12 months for ganglion development and integration
reversibility: Irreversible — ganglia integrate into existing nervous tissue
side_effects: Occasional involuntary movements from ganglion activity — fingers twitch, muscles flex without conscious command
The distributed ganglia develop rudimentary reflexes independent of brain control — the body 'flinches' before the brain registers a threat
Phantom sensations from ganglion processing of sensory data
Medical procedures affecting nerve tissue become more complex — ganglia must be mapped before surgery
Rare: ganglion network develops autonomous pain responses, causing unexplained pain signals from healthy tissue
social_perception: Elite and invisible. The modification is so expensive and so rare that encountering someone with distributed neural redundancy means encountering someone of extraordinary wealth or importance. The occasional involuntary finger twitches are the only visible sign.
story_hooks: A Starfish Spine user survives a spinal injury that should have killed them — their distributed ganglia kept their heart beating and their lungs working for three hours while emergency surgery was performed, and the surgeon had never seen the modification before

A Backup Brain user's ganglion network begins processing sensory data independently of the brain — the body is developing its own crude awareness, and it doesn't always agree with what the brain wants
